'''''Hildenbrandia rivularis''''' is a [[species]] of freshwater [[red algae]]. It forms red, crusty [[Thallus|thalli]] on stones submerged in water, typically in streams and rivers, less commonly in lakes and brackish parts of seas. It occurs in scattered locations on almost all continents. The species was formerly considered an indicator of clean or slightly polluted waters. The scientific genus name is sometimes spelled in various orthographic variants, especially as ''Hildenbrandtia''. The [[Biological life cycle|life cycle]] of this species was described by the Polish hydrobiologist {{Interlanguage link|Karol Starmach|pl|Karol Starmach}}.

== Structure ==

=== Habit ===
The thallus is in the form of a flat crust closely adhering to the rocky substrate, giving it the appearance of a coating. It grows radially, assuming a rounded, disc-like shape. It is composed of [[Cell (biology)|cells]] arranged in tightly fused vertical rows, with weakly branching. The lower layer of the thallus adheres to the substrate, without forming [[rhizoid]]s. The upper layer of the thallus is smooth.<ref name=":0">{{Cite web |title=Hildenbrandia rivularis (Liebmann) J.Agardh :: AlgaeBase |url=https://www.algaebase.org/search/species/detail/?species_id=G750a79520af28814 |access-date=2024-03-28 |website=www.algaebase.org}}</ref> The filaments of the vegetative thallus are strongly fused and difficult to separate. Forms similar to transections may develop at the edges of the thallus.<ref name=":1">{{Cite journal |last=Starmach |first=K. |year=1952 |title=O rozmnażaniu się krasnorosta Hildenbrandia rivularis (Liebm.) J. Ag. |url=https://pbsociety.org.pl/journals/index.php/asbp/article/view/asbp.1952.030/6465 |journal=Acta Societatis Botanicorum Poloniae |volume=21 |issue=3 |pages=447–474|doi=10.5586/asbp.1952.030 |doi-access=free }}</ref> The color is blood-red (from pink to burgundy),<ref name=":2">{{Cite book |last1=Szoszkiewicz |first1=Krzysztof |title=Klucz do oznaczania makrofitów dla potrzeb oceny stanu ekologicznego wód powierzchniowych |last2=Jusik |first2=Szymon |last3=Zgoła |first3=Tomasz |date=2010 |publisher=Inspekcja Ochrony Środowiska |isbn=978-83-61227-32-8 |edition= |series=Biblioteka Monitoringu Środowiska |location=Warsaw}}</ref> with a brownish hue in winter.<ref name=":3">{{Cite journal |last1=Żelazna-Wieczorek |first1=Joanna |last2=Ziułkiewicz |first2=Maciej |date=2011 |title=Hildenbrandia rivularis (Rhodophyta) in central Poland |url=https://pbsociety.org.pl/journals/index.php/asbp/article/view/asbp.2008.006 |journal=Acta Societatis Botanicorum Poloniae |volume=77 |issue=1 |pages=41–47 |doi=10.5586/asbp.2008.006 |issn=2083-9480|doi-access=free |bibcode=2011AcSBP..77...41Z }}</ref> Growth in thickness is limited, making it impossible to distinguish annual growth layers.<ref name=":4">{{Cite journal |last=Starmach |first=K. |year=1969 |title=Growth of thalli and reproduction of the red alga Hildenbrandia rivularis (Liebm.) J. Ag. |url=https://pbsociety.org.pl/journals/index.php/asbp/article/view/asbp.1969.044/4643 |journal=Acta Societatis Botanicorum Poloniae |volume=38 |issue=3 |pages=523–533|doi=10.5586/asbp.1969.044 |doi-access=free }}</ref>

Compared to other freshwater red algae, it exhibits relatively low [[Phenology|phenological]] variability,<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Kitayama |first=T. |year=2014 |title=Phenology and Morphology of the Two Freshwater Red Algae (Rhodophyta) in the Imperial Palace, Tokyo |url=https://www.kahaku.go.jp/research/researcher/papers/36415.pdf |journal=Memoirs of the National Museum of Nature and Science, Tokyo |volume=49 |pages=89–96}}</ref> while its eco-physiological parameters<ref name=":5">{{Cite journal |last1=Cantonati |first1=Marco |last2=Spitale |first2=Daniel |last3=Scalfi |first3=Alessia |last4=Guella |first4=Graziano |date=2016-03-30 |title=Exploring the contrasting seasonal strategies of two crenic macroalgae |journal=Fottea |volume=16 |issue=1 |pages=133–143 |doi=10.5507/fot.2015.029|doi-access=free }}</ref> and reproductive intensity vary depending on seasonal conditions.<ref name=":1" />

=== Anatomy ===
Anatomical features are quite variable. Initially, it was thought to be geographic variability, but in reality, the same variability occurs within local populations.<ref name=":4" /> Cells are approximately cylindrical to spherical. Individual cells contain single [[chloroplast]]s.<ref name=":0" /> Cells in different parts of the thallus have uneven sizes, varying even twofold, especially in the case of branching. The average size of cells is 8.4 × 8.6 μm, the average length of filaments is 38.4 μm, and the average thickness of the basal layer is 5.5 μm in the typical form, while in the variety distinguished by slightly darker coloration – ''Hildenbrandia rivularis'' var. ''drescheri'' Lingelsh. 1922 – these dimensions are respectively: 6.0 × 6.4 μm, 52.8 μm, 9.2 μm. Despite these differences, molecular studies do not indicate distinctiveness of this variety, and specimens classified as the species ''H. rivularis'' (at least those from [[Europe]] and the [[Canary Islands]]) show relatively low [[genetic variability]] compared to other traditionally recognized species of this genus.<ref name=":6">{{Cite journal |last1=Sherwood |first1=Alison R. |last2=Sheath |first2=Robert G. |year=2003 |title=Systematics of the Hildenbrandiales (Rhodophyta): gene sequence and morphometric analyses of global collections |url=https://onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/10.1046/j.1529-8817.2003.01050.x |journal=Journal of Phycology |language= |volume=39 |issue=2 |pages=409–422 |doi=10.1046/j.1529-8817.2003.01050.x |bibcode=2003JPcgy..39..409S |issn=0022-3646|url-access=subscription }}</ref> Despite the vivid red color of the entire thallus, individual cells may appear light green.<ref name=":7">{{Cite journal |last1=Caisová |first1=L. |last2=Kopecký |first2=J. |year=2008 |title=Relation of Pleurocapsa cuprea Hansgirg to the genus Hildenbrandia (Rhodophyta) |url=https://img.algaebase.org/pdf/AC1F1604111e82CEE9PW7987F575/43100.pdf |journal=Phycologia |volume=47 |issue=4 |pages=404–415 |doi=10.2216/PH07-70.1 |bibcode=2008Phyco..47..404C }}</ref>

=== Similar species ===
The most similar species is another freshwater representative of the genus – ''Hildenbrandia angolensis''. The range of anatomical dimensions of these two species overlaps, but on average, the cells of ''H. angolensis'' are smaller.<ref name=":6" /> A similar range of cell sizes is also found in the freshwater ''Hildenbrandia cuprea''. Its colonies form a crustose mat and are brick-red, while colonies of ''H. rivularis'' form a crustose, vivid red biofilm. Sometimes, the thalli of both species can be very similar to each other.<ref name=":7" />

It may be confused with other algae forming crustose thalli on rocks, such as the brown algae ''Heribaudiella fluviatilis''.<ref>{{Cite book |title=Freshwater algae of North America: ecology and classification |date=2003 |publisher=Academic Press |isbn=978-0-12-741550-5 |editor-last=Wehr |editor-first=John D. |location=Amsterdam; Boston |pages=757–773 |doi=10.1016/B978-012741550-5/50023-4 |editor-last2=Sheath |editor-first2=Robert G.}}</ref> In saline waters, including the entire [[Baltic Sea]], its variants are usually other species of ''Hildenbrandia'' (especially ''Hildenbrandia rubra''), although it may co-occur with them in the brackish [[Bothnian Bay]].<ref name=":8">{{Cite journal |year=2012 |title=Checklist of Baltic Sea Macro-species |url=https://www.yumpu.com/it/document/read/21897818/checklist-of-baltic-sea-macro-species-iow |journal=Baltic Sea Environment Proceedings |volume=130 |page=61 |issn=0357-2994}}</ref>

== Reproduction ==
The explanation of the [[Biological life cycle|life cycle]] of ''Hildenbrandia rivularis'' is considered one of {{Interlanguage link|Karol Starmach|lt=Karol Starmach's|pl|Karol Starmach}} most important discoveries.<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Gumiński |first=Stefan |year=1989 |title=Wspomnienie o Karolu Starmachu (22 IX 1900 — 2 III 1988) |url=https://pbsociety.org.pl/default/wp-content/uploads/2018/02/wb.1989.001_ev_s.pdf |journal=Wiadomości Botaniczne |language=pl |publisher=Instytut Botaniki PAN |volume=33 |issue=1 |pages=3–6 |archive-date=2018-04-25 |access-date=2024-03-28 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180425181125/https://pbsociety.org.pl/default/wp-content/uploads/2018/02/wb.1989.001_ev_s.pdf |url-status=dead }}</ref>

Freshwater species are exceptional within the genus ''Hildenbrandia'' because they do not produce [[tetraspore]]s and reproduce exclusively [[Asexual reproduction|asexually]].<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Pueschel |first=Curt M. |year=1982 |title=Ultrastructural observations of tetrasporangia and conceptacles in Hildenbrandia (rhodophyta: Hildenbrandiales) |url=http://www.tandfonline.com/doi/abs/10.1080/00071618200650331 |journal=British Phycological Journal |language= |volume=17 |issue=3 |pages=333–341 |doi=10.1080/00071618200650331 |issn=0007-1617|url-access=subscription }}</ref> This applies not only to ''Hildenbrandia rivularis'' but also to ''Hildenbrandia angolensis''.<ref name=":9">{{Cite journal |last1=Sherwood |first1=Alison R. |last2=Sheath |first2=Robert G. |year=2000 |title=Microscopic analysis and seasonality of gemma production in the freshwater red alga Hildenbrandia angolensis (Hildenbrandiales, Rhodophyta) |url=http://doi.wiley.com/10.1111/j.1440-1835.2000.tb00220.x |journal=Phycological Research |language= |volume=48 |issue=4 |pages=241–249 |doi=10.1111/j.1440-1835.2000.tb00220.x |doi-broken-date=5 July 2025 |issn=1322-0829|url-access=subscription }}</ref> Karol Starmach hypothesized that the reproductive organs [[Homology (biology)|homologous]] to the [[Tetrasporangium|tetrasporangia]] of other ''Hildenbrandia'' species are its [[Gemma (botany)|gemmae]],<ref name=":1" /> but this hypothesis has not been confirmed. Likewise, the presence of true tetrasporangia and the production of tetraspores reported in the 1950s have not been confirmed.<ref name=":9" />

According to observations by Starmach from the late 1920s, bright spots appear on the upper side of the thallus of ''Hildenbrandia rivularis'', which then grow into nodules and warts covered with a layer of [[mucus]]. For several decades, phycologists did not know their function.<ref name=":1" /> Theories were proposed that they could be [[Antheridium|antheridia]] or [[Oogonium|oogonia]] with trichogynes.<ref name=":4" /> In the late 1940s and early 1950s, Starmach conducted observations and experiments involving these structures, proving that they are gmmae. The gemmae consist of short (usually eight-celled) filaments arranged side by side, noticeably thicker than the filaments of the parent thallus (5–12 μm) and are relatively easy to separate. During their growth, their cells fill with [[starch]] at the expense of the space occupied by [[chloroplast]]s and swell. Their exterior becomes mucilaginous. Due to the compact arrangement of the filaments of the parent thallus, swelling causes the filaments to grow and protrude outward from the thallus. Mature gemmae are nodules with a diameter of up to 1 mm. These structures occur on the thallus year-round but develop most intensively in warm months, often when water levels are low, allowing rocks with thalli to protrude above the water. The gemmae detach, leaving small depressions in the thallus, and are carried away by the current. Upon contact with a substrate, they settle on it, adhere with mucus, and after two days, develop [[rhizoid]]s emerging from several basal cells. These rhizoids do not contain chloroplasts. Under favorable conditions, some rhizoids branch, and new chloroplast-containing cells develop at their tips, giving rise to new thalli. In unfavorable conditions, such as winter, this process takes several weeks. After a few more days, the cells of the gemmae die, as do the older parts of the rhizoids, and the newly formed thalli grow radially on the substrate. The development of new crustose thalli requires the apex cell of the rhizoid to come into contact with a hard substrate, while on a soft substrate, filaments that do not form typical thalli develop. In such cases, a form resembling ''{{Interlanguage link|Chantransia|lt=|pl|Szantransja}}'' may rarely appear, which over time may transform into a typical thallus.<ref name=":1" />

Gemmae and thallus fragments usually flow downstream, and upstream transport likely occurs through animals such as [[leech]]es<ref name=":4" /> or [[Chironomidae]]'s larvae.<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Starmach |first=K. |year=1988 |title=Nowsze dane o krasnorostach |url=http://mbc.malopolska.pl/Content/122411/kosmos_1988_001.pdf |journal=[[Kosmos. Problemy Nauk Biologicznych]] |volume=37 |issue=1 |pages=91–113}}</ref>

Reproduction through thallus fragmentation, i.e., the regeneration of a new thallus from a piece of old thallus not being a gemma, also occurs but is less common in natural conditions. In such cases, rhizoids or thread-like forms resembling ''Chantransia'' may not form.<ref name=":1" />

Another relatively rare form of vegetative reproduction is the formation of filaments resembling [[stolon]]s, on which new thalli develop at the ends. These stolons have been described as ''Chantransia hildenbrandtiae''.<ref name=":4" />

== Ecology and occurrence ==

=== Distribution ===
The species is freshwater, although it also occurs in the most brackish waters of the [[Baltic Sea]] – the [[Bothnian Bay]] and its surroundings ([[Archipelago Sea]]).<ref name=":8" /> Its presence has been recorded in almost the whole of [[Europe]], including the [[Caucasus]], the basin of the [[Caribbean Sea]], eastern [[Asia]], the [[Congo Basin]], eastern [[Australia]], and [[New Zealand]].<ref name=":0" /> Records in [[North America]] may actually refer to ''Hildenbrandia angolensis''.<ref name=":16">{{Cite journal |last1=Sheath |first1=Robert G. |last2=Kaczmarczyk |first2=Donald |last3=Cole |first3=Kathleen M. |year=1993 |title=Distribution and systematics of freshwater Hildenbrandia (Rhodophyta, Hildenbrandiales) in North America |url=http://www.tandfonline.com/doi/abs/10.1080/09670269300650191 |journal=European Journal of Phycology |language= |volume=28 |issue=2 |pages=115–121 |doi=10.1080/09670269300650191 |bibcode=1993EJPhy..28..115S |issn=0967-0262|url-access=subscription }}</ref>

In some 20th-century sources, it was considered a common species in [[Poland]], especially in the north and in the [[Carpathian Mountains]].<ref name=":10">{{Cite book |last=Starmach |first=Karol |title=Phaeophyta – brunatnice, Rhodophyta – krasnorosty |publisher=Państwowe Wydawnictwo Naukowe |year=1977 |series=Flora słodkowodna Polski |volume=14 |location=Warsaw, Kraków |pages=253–254}}</ref> According to other studies, it occurs in scattered locations in Poland – mainly in [[Pomerania]], less frequently in the [[Beskids]], and until the 21st century, it was almost unheard of in central Poland.<ref name=":3" /> Since then, additional occurrences have been noted,<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Smoczyk |first=M. |year=2011 |title=Nowe stanowiska Hildenbrandia Rivularis (Liebm.) J. Agardh (Rhodophyta) w województwie lubuskim |url=https://www.kp.org.pl/pdf/pp/pdf2/PP_4_Notatki.pdf |journal=Przegląd Przyrodniczy |volume=XXII |issue=4}}</ref> and it can now be found in almost every part of Poland.<ref name=":2" /> In the 21st century, apart from the northern, western, and mountainous parts of Poland, it has been recorded in isolated locations. During this period, there has been a multiple increase in the number of known habitats, accompanied by the disappearance of historical mountain habitats.<ref name=":11">{{Cite journal |last1=Jakubas-Krzak |first1=Emilia |last2=Gąbka |first2=Maciej |last3=Panek |first3=Piotr |last4=W. A. Kowalski |first4=Wojciech |last5=Lisek |first5=Daniel |last6=Smoczyk |first6=Michał |last7=Rybak |first7=Andrzej S. |year=2023 |title=The red alga Hildenbrandia rivularis is a weak indicator of the good ecological status of riverine habitats |journal=Ecological Indicators |language= |volume=147 |pages=109–918 |article-number=109918 |doi=10.1016/j.ecolind.2023.109918|bibcode=2023EcInd.14709918J |doi-access=free }}</ref>

=== Autecology ===
[[Lithophyte]], a component of the [[phytobenthos]], has a relatively broad [[ecological tolerance]],<ref name=":11" /> although it prefers swiftly flowing rivers with relatively clean water.<ref name=":2" /> It favors shaded areas but can also occur in sun-exposed locations.<ref name=":11" /> The crusty shape of its thallus allows it to fit into the [[boundary layer]], where the current has less effect. ''Hildenbrandia'' more often covers the parts of rocks facing the current. It grows in waters with various flow velocities, averaging 32 cm/s, which qualifies it as a [[rheophile]].<ref name=":12">{{Cite book |last1=Kawecka |first1=Barbara |title=Zarys ekologii glonów wód słodkich i środowisk lądowych |last2=Eloranta |first2=Pertti Vesa |date=1994 |publisher=Wydaw. Naukowe PWN |isbn=978-83-01-11320-9 |location=Warsaw |pages=86–87, 212}}</ref> However, it is also found in slower-flowing and stagnant waters.<ref name=":11" /> The presence of hard, mineral substrate is crucial for the settling and development of ''Hildenbrandia''. Therefore, it often occurs on [[knickpoint]]s, boulders, gravel, as well as on artificial substrates like the infrastructure of [[watermill]]s.<ref name=":1" /> It can also settle on [[seashell]]s or glass.<ref name=":4" /> Swift flow promotes water self-purification, especially from easily oxidizable organic [[Water pollution|pollutants]], thus ''Hildenbrandia rivularis'' is considered an [[saprobic system]] for clean waters: xenosaprobic and oligosaprobic.<ref name=":13">{{Cite journal |last1=Eloranta |first1=Pertti |last2=Kwandrans |first2=Janina |year=2004 |title=Indicator value of freshwater red algae in running waters for water quality assessment |url=http://www.oandhs.org/files/60.pdf |journal=Oceanological and Hydrobiological Studies |publisher=Uniwersytet Gdański, Instytut Oceanografii |volume=33 |issue=1 |issn=1730-413X |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120314084750/http://www.oandhs.org/files/60.pdf |archive-date=2012-03-14 |access-date=2024-03-28 |url-status=live }}</ref> It is somewhat less sensitive to excess [[Mineral (nutrient)|minerals]], tolerating elevated nitrogen content but not high phosphorus content. It occurs over a wide range of specific electrolytic conductivity (a measure of dissolved mineral substances).<ref name=":3" /> It is found in waters with a slightly acidic to slightly alkaline pH, although it is more common in alkaline waters, hence it is described as an [[alkaliphile]]. This preference is also associated with [[hard water]]. Despite this, it tends to cover [[acidic rock]]s with low calcium content,<ref name=":13" /><ref name=":1" /> although it is also found in [[limestone]] quarries.<ref name=":1" /><ref>{{Cite journal |last=Nichols |first=H. Wayne |year=1965 |title=Culture and Development of Hildenbrandia rivularis from Denmark and North America |url=https://www.jstor.org/stable/2439969 |journal=American Journal of Botany |publisher=Botanical Society of America |volume=52 |issue=1 |pages=9–15|doi=10.2307/2439969 |jstor=2439969 |url-access=subscription }}</ref> In alpine streams, it dominates warm waters in the summer – both nutrient-poor and calcium-rich.<ref name=":12" /> It is a [[eurytherm]]ic species but prefers warm waters.<ref name=":1" />

It can also occur in stagnant waters. In such an environment, it prefers shaded areas with fairly strong wave action.<ref name=":3" /> In [[Lake Constance]], it was recorded at depths of 8–45 m,<ref name=":4" /> and in [[Lake Garda]], even up to 90 m.<ref name=":10" />

=== Bioindicators ===
Freshwater red algae, including ''Hildenbrandia rivularis'', are considered [[bioindicator]]s of water cleanliness. However, among them, it is recognized as a species relatively tolerant to pollution.<ref name=":14">{{Cite journal |last1=Jakubas |first1=Emilia |last2=Gąbka |first2=Maciej |last3=Joniak |first3=Tomasz |year=2014 |title=Factors Determining the Distribution of Reophil and Protected Hildenbrandia rivularis (Liebmann) J. Agardh 1851, the Rhodophyta Freshwater Species, in Lowland River Ecosystems |url=http://www.bioone.org/doi/10.3161/104.062.0412 |journal=Polish Journal of Ecology |language= |volume=62 |issue=4 |pages=679–693 |doi=10.3161/104.062.0412 |issn=1505-2249|url-access=subscription }}</ref> In German literature, it falls into categories of indicators for fertile waters: meso-eutrophic or eu-politrophic and β-mesosaprobic, indicating moderately polluted waters. As a [[Trophic level|trophic]] indicator, it has relatively low significance, but as a [[saprobic system]], it holds relatively high importance.<ref name=":15">{{Cite journal |last1=Täuscher |first1=L. |last2=Krumbiegel |first2=A. |year=2020 |title=Erstfunde der Krusten-Rotalge Hildenbrandia rivularis (Liebmann) J. G. Agardh und der Krusten-Braunalge Heribaudiella fluviatilis (Areschoug) Svedelius im Tangelnschen Bach (Sachsen-Anhalt, Deutschland) |url=http://botanischer-verein-sachsen-anhalt.de/wp-content/uploads/2021/01/Flo-Kart_2020_19-30_Taeuscher_Krumbiegel.pdf |journal=Mitteilungen zur Floristischen Kartierung in Sachsen-Anhalt |language=de |volume=25 |pages=19–30|doi=10.21248/mfk.35 }}</ref> In those types of watercourses where it is significant as an indicator, it is classified as a non-diatom [[phytobenthos]] species in category B, meaning it is less sensitive than taxa requiring the best environmental conditions.<ref>{{Cite book |last=Schaumburg |first=J. |url=https://www.gewaesser-bewertung.de/files/verfahrensanleitung_fg.pdf |title=Verfahrensanleitung für die ökologische Bewertung von Fließgewässern zur Umsetzung der EG-Wasserrahmenrichtlinie: Makrophyten und Phytobenthos. Phylib |publisher=Bayerisches Landesamt für Umwelt |year=2012 |page=94 |language=de |access-date=2024-03-28 |archive-date=2021-09-13 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210913112643/https://www.gewaesser-bewertung.de/files/verfahrensanleitung_fg.pdf |url-status=dead }}</ref> In Poland, it is taken into account when determining the {{Interlanguage link|River Macrophyte Index|lt=|pl|Makrofitowy Indeks Rzeczny}}, with values of W=6 (indicating a preference for mesotrophic waters) and L=2 (indicating an average tolerance range).<ref>{{Cite book |url=https://www.worldcat.org/title/1225221050 |title=Podręcznik do monitoringu elementów biologicznych i klasyfikacji stanu ekologicznego wód powierzchniowych: aktualizacja metod |date=2020 |publisher=Główny Inspektorat Ochrony Środowiska |isbn=978-83-950881-2-4 |editor-last=Kolada |editor-first=Agnieszka |series=Biblioteka Monitoringu Środowiska |location=Warsaw |page=111 |oclc=1225221050 |editor-last2=Adamczyk |editor-first2=Mikołaj |editor-last3=Bielczyńska |editor-first3=Aleksandra |editor-last4=Bis |editor-first4=Barbara |editor-last5=Błachuta |editor-first5=Jan |editor-last6=Błeńska |editor-first6=Magdalena |editor-last7=Bociąg |editor-first7=Katarzyna |editor-last8=Brzeska-Roszczyk |editor-first8=Paulina |editor-last9=Ciecierska |editor-first9=Hanna}}</ref> Due to its broader ecological tolerance than previously believed, its bioindicative value is questioned.<ref name=":11" />

=== Interspecies interactions and phytosociology ===
Occupying habitats where it is difficult for other organisms to settle allows ''Hildenbrandia rivularis'' to avoid [[Competition (biology)|competition]],<ref name=":4" /> although its ecological niche may overlap with that occupied by ''Heribaudiella fluviatilis''.<ref name=":14" /> It happens that specimens of this species overgrow ''Hildenbrandia'' individuals.<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Fritsch |first=F. E. |year=1929 |title=The Encrusting Algal Communities of Certain Fast-Flowing Streams |url=https://nph.onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/pdf/10.1111/j.1469-8137.1929.tb06754.x |journal=The New Phytologist |volume=28 |issue=3 |pages=165–196|doi=10.1111/j.1469-8137.1929.tb06754.x |url-access=subscription }}</ref> Mosses such as ''Leptodictyum riparium'', ''Fontinalis antipyretica'', ''Hygroamblystegium tenax'', or ''Rhynchostegium confertum'', as well as lichens like ''Verrucaria elaeomelaena'' or ''Verrucaria rheitrophila'', may also occur in similar habitats.<ref name=":5" /> It relatively often occurs near habitats of [[Nuphar lutea|yellow water-lily]], [[Sagittaria sagittifolia|arrowhead]], and [[Potamogeton crispus|crisp-leaved pondweed]].<ref name=":11" />

The surface of Hildenbrandia thallus is colonized by various epiphytic organisms, such as the diatom Cocconeis lineata. Thalli may be grazed upon by insect larvae (e.g., chironomids) or snails, but this phenomenon usually does not cause significant damage.

The plant community formed by ''Hildenbrandia rivularis'' is referred to as the ''Hildenbrandietum rivularis'' {{Interlanguage link|Phytoassociation|lt=phytoassociation|pl|Zespół roślinności}} (Luther 1954). It was also described as the non-rank association ''Hildenbrandia-Lithoderma'' (Fritsch 1929), redefined as the ''Hildenbrandio rivularis-Heribaudielletum fluviatilis'' (Fritsch 1929 corr. Täuscher). It belongs to the class of crustose communities or mats of epilithic algae ''Lemaneetea''.<ref name=":15" /><ref>{{Cite web |title=UC (LEF) - Lemaneetea fluviatilis Weber-Oldecop ex Bobrov et Chemeris 2012 |url=https://www.synbiosys.alterra.nl/evc/vegtype.aspx?selectnode=false&vegtype=3UC |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210912161256/https://www.synbiosys.alterra.nl/evc/vegtype.aspx?selectnode=false&vegtype=3UC |archive-date=2021-09-12}}</ref> In another system, the ''Rheithrophilo-Hildenbrandietum'' phytoassociation is distinguished, composed of ''Hildenbrandia rivularis'', ''Verrucaria rheitrophila'', and cyanobacteria such as ''Chamaesiphon polonicus'' and ''Chamaesiphon fuscus''.<ref>{{Cite book |last1=Podbielkowski |first1=Zbigniew |title=Zarys hydrobotaniki |last2=Tomaszewicz |first2=Henryk |date=1996 |publisher=Wydaw. Naukowe PWN |isbn=978-83-01-00566-5 |edition= |location=Warsaw |page=480}}</ref>

Exceptionally, ''Hildenbrandia rivularis'' can occupy habitats typical for marine species, such as ''Hildenbrandia rubra''. This occurs in the most freshwater areas of the Baltic Sea (Bothnian Bay).<ref>{{Cite book |url=http://link.springer.com/10.1007/978-94-007-0668-2 |title=Biological Oceanography of the Baltic Sea |date=2017 |publisher=Springer Netherlands |isbn=978-94-007-0667-5 |editor-last=Snoeijs-Leijonmalm |editor-first=Pauline |location=Dordrecht |page=423 |language=en |doi=10.1007/978-94-007-0668-2 |editor-last2=Schubert |editor-first2=Hendrik |editor-last3=Radziejewska |editor-first3=Teresa}}</ref>

== Threats and preservation ==
In Poland, ''Hildenbrandia rivularis'' has been under species protection since 2004 (as one of the few [[algae]] species outside the [[charales]] group).<ref>The Regulation of the Minister of the Environment of 9 July 2004, on species of wild plants protected by law was published in the Journal of Laws of 2004, No. 168, item 1764.</ref><ref>The Regulation of the Minister of the Environment of 9 October 2014, concerning the protection of plant species was published in the Journal of Laws of 2014, item 1409.</ref> It is listed on the {{Interlanguage link|Red list of algae in Poland|lt=red list of algae in Poland|pl|Czerwona lista roślin i grzybów Polski}} with a status of '''V''' – [[vulnerable species]].<ref>{{Cite book |last=Siemińska |first=Jadwiga |title=Lista roślin zagrożonych w Polsce |publisher=Instytut Botaniki im. W. Szafera PAN |year=1992 |editor-last=Zarzycki |editor-first=K. |location=Kraków |pages=7–19 |chapter=Czerwona lista glonów zagrożonych w Polsce |editor-last2=Wojewoda |editor-first2=W. |editor-last3=Heinrich |editor-first3=Z.}}</ref> It is also included in the red book of plants of [[Belarus]].<ref>{{Cite book |title=Беларуская энцыклапедыя |publisher=Беларуская Энцыклапедыя імя Петруся Броўкі |year=1996 |isbn=985-11-0061-7 |editor-last=Пашкоў |editor-first=Г.П. |series=Аршыца Беларусцы |volume=2 |location=Minsk |page=157 |language=be |chapter=Ахоўныя расліны}}</ref> In the red list of [[Finland]] in 2019, it was classified as '''NT''' – [[near-threatened species]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Punaisen kirjan verkkopalvelu |url=https://punainenkirja.laji.fi/results/MX.292205?checklist=MR.424 |access-date=2024-03-28 |website=punainenkirja.laji.fi}}</ref>

Being a shade-tolerant species, its habitats are threatened by the cutting of [[riparian forest]]s.<ref name=":1" />

The habitat of ''Hildenbrandia rivularis'' on a hundred-meter stretch of stream in the [[Ślęża Landscape Park]] has been established as a [[natural monument]] called ''Red Algae'' ({{Langx|pl|Krasnorost}}).<ref>{{Cite web |title=Formy ochrony przyrody - Dolnośląski Zespół Parków Krajobrazowych |url=http://dzpk.pl/pl/parki-krajobrazowe/95-slezanski-park-krajobrazowy/167-formy-ochrony.html |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190129110841/http://dzpk.pl/pl/parki-krajobrazowe/95-slezanski-park-krajobrazowy/167-formy-ochrony.html |archive-date=2019-01-29 |access-date=2018-09-13 |website=dzpk.pl |language=pl}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=2018-10-07 |title=Pomnik Przyrody Krasnorost - Przyroda Dolnego Śląska |url=https://przyrodniczo.pl/cenne-tereny/krasnorost/ |access-date=2024-03-28 |language=pl-PL}}</ref>

== Systematics and origins ==
It is assumed that its ancestors were marine algae.<ref name=":1" /> According to initial [[Hypothesis|hypotheses]], the transition to freshwater occurred in the [[Tertiary period|Tertiary]] period or earlier.<ref name=":4" /> Another hypothesis suggested that various subpopulations originated from multiple independent transitions of the marine form to inland water. In the case of populations in the Baltic Sea basin, this would only be possible after the retreat of the glacier, i.e., during the [[Holocene]]. The parent species could be ''Hildenbrandia rubra'', which inhabits {{Interlanguage link|Transitional waters|lt=transitional waters|pl|Wody przejściowe}} in the Baltic Sea, among other places. With multiple invasions, genetic differentiation of European subpopulations could be expected, stemming from different parent populations. However, in reality, populations of ''Hildenbrandia rivularis'' are very homogeneous, suggesting that there was a single invasion from saltwater. Furthermore, genetic distinctiveness from marine species indicates that it has a history predating the end of the [[Weichselian glaciation]].<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Sherwood |first1=A. R. |last2=Shea |first2=T. B. |last3=Sheath |first3=R. G. |year=2002 |title=European freshwater Hildenbrandia (Hildenbrandiales, Rhodophyta) has not been derived from multiple invasions from marine habitats |url=https://www.tandfonline.com/doi/full/10.2216/i0031-8884-41-1-87.1 |journal=Phycologia |volume=41 |issue=1 |pages=87–95 |doi=10.2216/i0031-8884-41-1-87.1 |bibcode=2002Phyco..41...87S |access-date=2021-09-11|url-access=subscription }}</ref>

''Hildenbrandia rivularis'' shows low [[genetic variability]],<ref name=":6" /> which may result from the fact that it reproduces only asexually.<ref name=":4" /> For several decades, a variety called ''Hildenbrandia rivularis'' var. ''drescheri'' (Lingelsheim 1922) was distinguished, with [[Ligota Wielka, Nysa County|Ligota Wielka]] near [[Otmuchów]] as its type locality.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Guiry |first=M. D. |year=2017 |title=Hildenbrandia rivularis var. drescheri Lingelsheim 1922 |url=https://www.algaebase.org/search/species/detail/?species_id=116687 |access-date=2021-09-12 |website=AlgaeBase}}</ref> In phycological tradition, such distinguished varieties are treated almost on par with separate species. This variety has slightly larger cells and a darker shade. Molecular studies do not indicate the distinctiveness of this taxon, and since 2003, it has not been distinguished.<ref name=":6" /> Based on morphological and ecological differences, a subspecies occurring in the [[Mecsek]] mountains, ''Hildenbrandia rivularis'' subsp. ''chalikophila'' (Palik 1961), was distinguished, initially described as a separate species, ''Hildenbrandia chalikophila'' (Palik 1957).<ref>{{Cite journal |year=1957 |title=Studien über Hildenbrandia rivularis (Liebm.) J. Ag. |url=https://img.algaebase.org/pdf/AC1F1D7019140285DFNs9BF41505/47099.pdf |journal=Annales Universitatis Scientiarum Budapestinensis de Rolando Eötvös Nominatae. Sectio Biologica 1 |language=de |pages=205–218}}</ref>

Both morphologically and genetically, the most similar are two other species of freshwater ''Hildenbrandia'': ''Hildenbrandia angolensis'' and ''Hildenbrandia cuprea''. The latter species was recognized for many years as a [[Cyanobacteria|cyanobacterium]] under the name ''Pleurocapsa cuprea''.<ref>{{Citation |last=Kumano |first=Shigeru |chapter=Taxonomic Revisions of Freshwater Rhodophyta in Recent Years |date=2010 |title=Red Algae in the Genomic Age |series=Cellular Origin, Life in Extreme Habitats and Astrobiology |volume=13 |pages=111–125 |editor-last=Seckbach |editor-first=Joseph |chapter-url=https://link.springer.com/10.1007/978-90-481-3795-4_6 |access-date=2024-03-28 |place=Dordrecht |publisher=Springer Netherlands |language=en |doi=10.1007/978-90-481-3795-4_6 |isbn=978-90-481-3794-7 |editor2-last=Chapman |editor2-first=David J.|chapter-url-access=subscription }}</ref> Another freshwater species, ''Hildenbrandia ramanaginae'', occurs in [[India]] but is poorly described and is not included in molecular analyses allowing for the determination of relatedness.<ref name=":16" /><ref name=":9" />

In addition to the genus ''Hildenbrandia'' in the family ''Hildenbrandiaceae'', the genus ''Apophlaea'' is distinguished. However, molecular data indicate that its [[clade]] is nested within the ''Hildenbrandia'' clade, so it could be eliminated.<ref name=":6" /> In such a case, the family ''Hildenbrandiaceae'' would be [[Monotypic taxon|monotypic]]. Moreover, subsequent taxa at higher ranks up to the level of subclass ''Hildenbrandiophyceae'' are also monotypic.<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Ruggiero |first=Michael A. |date=2015-04-29 |editor-last=Thuesen |editor-first=Erik V. |title=A Higher Level Classification of All Living Organisms |journal=PLOS ONE |language= |volume=10 |issue=4 |article-number=e0119248 |doi=10.1371/journal.pone.0119248 |doi-access=free |issn=1932-6203 |pmc= 4418965|pmid=25923521|bibcode=2015PLoSO..1019248R }}</ref> Therefore, in cladistic classification systems, the family ''Hildenbrandiaceae'' is a distinct clade from other clades at the rank of subclass, emerging with them from the node ''Florideophycidae''.<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Adl |first=Sina M. |year=2019 |title=Revisions to the Classification, Nomenclature, and Diversity of Eukaryotes |journal=Journal of Eukaryotic Microbiology |language=en |volume=66 |issue=1 |pages=4–119 |doi=10.1111/jeu.12691 |issn=1066-5234 |pmc=6492006 |pmid=30257078}}</ref>

=== Name ===
The generic name in the form of ''Hildbrandtia'' was coined in 1834 by Giandomenico Nardo, commemorating the Viennese doctor of medicine and botany Hildbrandt (''cui nomen venit a clarissimo doctore Hildbrandt Vindobonensi, clinico illustri, ac Botanico peritissimo'').<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Nardo |first=G. D. |year=1834 |title=De novo genere Algarum cui nomen est Hildbrandtia prototypus |url=https://img.algaebase.org/pdf/562DF314141862F8F3NuQ11CF46B/17192.pdf |journal=Isis von Oken |language=it |pages=675–676}}</ref> Most likely, it refers to Franz Xaver Edler von Hildenbrand (1789–1849).<ref>{{Cite web |last=Hansson |first=H. G. |title=Biographical Etymology of Marine Organism Names. H |url=https://www.bemon.loven.gu.se/petymol.h.html |access-date=2024-03-28 |website=www.bemon.loven.gu.se}}</ref><ref name=":17">{{Cite journal |last=Widder |first=F. |year=1958 |title=Der Gattungsname Hildenbrandia |url=https://www.zobodat.at/pdf/PHY_7_4_0315-0320.pdf |journal=Phyton |volume=7 |pages=315–320}}</ref> Hence, in the literature, from the very beginning, various versions of the name were used, such as ''Hildebrandtia'', ''Hildenbrandia'', ''Hildenbrandtia'', and ''Hildenbrantia''. The term ''Hildenbrandia'' was proposed in 1840 by Giovanni Zanardini and over time, especially since the 1950s, it became dominant (after identifying the person commemorated by this name).<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Silva |first=Paul C. |date=1980 |title=Remarks on algal nomenclature VI |url=https://onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/10.2307/1219605 |journal=Taxon |language= |volume=29 |issue=1 |pages=121–145 |doi=10.2307/1219605 |jstor=1219605 |issn=0040-0262|url-access=subscription }}</ref><ref name=":17" />

The species was first scientifically described by Frederik Michael Liebmann in a work from 1838 based on [[Holotype|holotypic]] specimens collected by Statsraada Hornemann in 1826 in a stream at Kongens Møller in [[Zealand]] (type locality). He then assigned it the name ''Erythroclathrus rivularis'', noting that it refers to algae also described as ''Palmella rubra'' or ''Verrucaria rubra''.<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Liebmann |first=Frederik Michael |year=1838 |title=Om et nyt genus Erythroclathrus af algernes familie |url=http://img.algaebase.org/pdf/AC100CF102dbf22F7Ettk366085D/18870.pdf |journal=Naturhistorisk Tidsskrift |language=nl |volume=2 |issue=1 |pages=169–175}}</ref> The [[binomial nomenclature]] ''rivularis'' has a Latin origin and is often given to species associated with streams.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Glossary> Rivularis (rivulare) |url=https://www.algaebase.org/search/glossary/?actionis=search&term=rivularis |access-date=2024-03-28 |website=www.algaebase.org}}</ref> Subsequently, the same species was described by Giovanni Zanardini as ''Hildenbrandia paroliniana''<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Zanardini |first=G. |year=1840 |title=Alia Direzione della Biblioteca Italiana |url=https://img.algaebase.org/pdf/AC1F2927027ed1DFDBXiCA0A48B5/17840.pdf |journal=Biblioteca Italiana |language=it |volume=96 |pages=131–137}}</ref> and by Louis Alphonse de Brébisson as ''Hildenbrandia fluviatilis'' (without the required taxonomic diagnosis). In 1849, [[Friedrich Traugott Kützing]]<ref>{{Cite book |last=Kützing |first=F. T. |url=https://img.algaebase.org/pdf/8CCB0C030779a1D85AuRCC021765/13490.pdf |title=Species algarum |publisher=F. A. Brockhaus |year=1849 |location=Lipsk |page=695 |language=la}}</ref> recognized that these were the same taxa, simultaneously considering them a riverine variety of ''Hildebrandtia rosea'', i.e., ''Hildenbrandtia rosea'' var. ''fluviatilis''. In 1851, Jakob Georg Agardh transferred the species under the current name, then written as ''Hildenbrandtia rivularis''.<ref>{{Cite book |last=Agardh |first=Jakob Georg |url=http://img.algaebase.org/pdf/562E29E502c93313FFVqo1077CC7/12265.pdf |title=Species genera et ordines algarum, seu descriptiones succinctae specierum, generum et ordinum, quibus algarum regnum constituitur. Volumen secundum: algas florideas complectens. Part 2, fasc. 1. |year=1851 |pages=337–351, 351–506}}</ref>

== Cultural significance ==
By covering [[flint]]stones with a durable pink color, ''Hildenbrandia'' may have influenced the perception of places where this phenomenon occurs (e.g., [[Stonehenge]]) as magical.<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Jacques |first1=David |last2=Phillips |first2=Tom |year=2014 |title=Mesolithic settlement near Stonehenge: excavations at Blick Mead, Vespasian's Camp, Amesbury |url=http://www.silversaffron.co.uk/wp-content/uploads/2014/07/02_Jacques_VespasiansCamp.pdf |journal=Wiltshire Archaeological & Natural History Magazine |volume=107 |pages=7–27}}</ref>
